Learn to explain how to share Swift code between apps with a package: Swift Package, Package Manifest & Library Product, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Swift Package - A folder of Swift code and a manifest file that you can share and reuse in many apps.
Package Manifest - The Package.swift file that lists the package name, its products, its targets and its dependencies.
Library Product - The part of a package that other packages and apps can import and use.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Swift Package, Package Manifest and Library Product in English?

dialogue.title: Stop copying the code

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, we copy the networking code into every app. Is there a better way?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, make a Swift package. A Swift package is a folder of Swift code that many apps can reuse.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What makes the folder a package?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The package manifest. It is the Package.swift file, and `package` is its main value.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What goes inside the package manifest?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The name, the `products`, the `targets` and the dependencies.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And a product is what other apps import?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. A library product is the part of a package that others can import.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So `.library` makes the library product for `Kit`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Without a library product, no app can import your code.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can one Swift package have more than one library product?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Split it by feature, so each app imports only what it needs.

dialogue.code:
import PackageDescription
let package = Package(name: "Kit", products: [
    .library(name: "Kit", targets: ["Kit"])],
    targets: [.target(name: "Kit")])
